title: Structure of Health Facilities and Social Services
path: Structure of Health Facilities and Social Services

headings.title: Introduction to Healthcare Delivery Systems in Nigeria
headings.content:
The healthcare delivery system in Nigeria operates on a three-tier structure designed to provide comprehensive services from the grassroots to specialized national centers. This decentralized framework divides responsibilities among the federal, state, and local government tiers. Federal authorities manage tertiary institutions and national health policies, state ministries oversee secondary hospitals and general health administration, while local government councils shoulder the primary responsibility for community-level care.

Understanding this hierarchy helps healthcare providers navigate resource distribution, referral channels, and administrative bottlenecks. Primary facilities handle basic preventative and curative needs, secondary facilities manage more complex medical and surgical cases requiring hospital admission, and tertiary centers provide highly specialized care alongside clinical training and research. Resource disparities often exist between urban and rural settings, making functional inter-facility communication vital for patient survival.

headings.title: Primary Health Facilities
headings.content:
Primary health facilities represent the first point of contact for individuals, families, and communities within the national health system. These centers bring health services as close as possible to where people live and work. Facilities at this level include health posts, health clinics, and comprehensive health centers.

Services provided here focus heavily on disease prevention, health promotion, and basic curative interventions. Key activities include:

- **Immunization**: Administering routine vaccines against childhood killer diseases.
- **Maternal and Child Health**: Providing antenatal care, supervised normal deliveries, and postnatal follow-ups.
- **Nutritional Support**: Monitoring growth and managing uncomplicated malnutrition.
- **Basic Treatment**: Managing common tropical ailments like uncomplicated malaria, diarrheal diseases, and minor injuries.

Staffing typically consists of community health extension workers, nurses, midwives, and primary health care tutors, with occasional visits from medical officers.

headings.title: Secondary Health Facilities
headings.content:
Secondary health facilities provide specialized care for patients referred from primary health centers. These institutions typically take the form of general hospitals, comprehensive health centers, or state specialist hospitals managed by state ministries of health.

When a patient's condition exceeds the diagnostic or therapeutic capabilities of a primary clinic, they are sent to a secondary facility. These hospitals feature specialized departments staffed by medical officers, general surgeons, pediatricians, obstetricians and gynecologists, pharmacists, and professional nurses.

| Facility Level | Typical Staffing Focus | Core Operational Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary | CHEWs, Nurses, Midwives | Prevention, health education, basic curative care |
| Secondary | General Practitioners, Specialists, Nurses | Inpatient admission, surgery, diagnostic imaging |

Inpatient wards, operating theatres, laboratories, and X-ray units are standard features here. They handle emergency obstetric care, major trauma stabilization, surgical operations like appendectomies and caesarean sections, and the management of acute medical crises.

headings.title: Tertiary Health Facilities
headings.content:
Tertiary health facilities represent the apex of the healthcare delivery pyramid, offering highly specialized medical, surgical, and diagnostic services. Teaching hospitals and federal medical centers are prime examples, usually affiliated with universities for medical and nursing education.

Patients reach this level through formal referral channels from secondary hospitals when they require advanced sub-specialty intervention. These institutions house advanced intensive care units, neurosurgery units, cardiothoracic services, oncology departments, and sophisticated laboratory diagnostics.

Beyond specialized clinical care, tertiary centers serve as hubs for medical research and professional training. Consultants across various disciplines lead teams of resident doctors, specialist nurses, and allied health professionals. While they handle the most complex and critical health challenges, their heavy patient loads can sometimes lead to congestion if lower-level facilities do not properly filter routine cases.

headings.title: Social Services and Community Support
headings.content:
Healthcare extends far beyond the physical walls of clinics and hospitals; it is deeply intertwined with social welfare systems. Social services address the non-medical determinants of health, including poverty, homelessness, domestic abuse, disability, and social isolation. Medical social workers operate within hospitals to link patients with community resources, financial aid, and legal assistance.

In many Nigerian communities, social services also involve non-governmental organizations, religious bodies, and traditional support structures that cushion vulnerable populations against catastrophic health spending. When a patient cannot afford prescribed medications or requires long-term rehabilitation after a stroke, social service departments intervene to arrange charity support, foster care, or placement in specialized homes. Nurses must collaborate closely with social workers to ensure that discharge plans account for the patient's home environment and socio-economic reality.

headings.title: Inter-Referral Pathways and Continuity of Care
headings.content:
An effective referral system ensures that patients move smoothly between primary, secondary, and tertiary levels of care based on their clinical needs. Referral is a two-way process: upward referral occurs when a patient requires a higher level of expertise or equipment, while downward referral sends a stable patient back to a primary facility for follow-up and maintenance care, freeing up tertiary beds.

Clear communication is the bedrock of this process. Every referral must be accompanied by a comprehensive referral letter detailing the patient's history, findings, tentative diagnosis, treatments administered, and the specific reason for transfer. Breakdowns in this pathway lead to overcrowded tertiary wards, delayed interventions, and fragmented patient experiences. Maintaining continuity of care protects patients from falling through the cracks of a complex health architecture.

headings.title: The Role of Nurses Across Different Facility Levels
headings.content:
Professional nursing practice adapts dynamically across the various tiers of the Nigerian health system. At the primary level, nurses often function as generalists, educators, and community health leaders. They run immunization clinics, conduct home visits, manage normal pregnancies, and train community health workers.

In secondary hospitals, the nursing role shifts toward acute inpatient care, perioperative management in surgical suites, and emergency stabilization. Nurses coordinate daily ward activities, administer complex medication regimens, and monitor postoperative recovery.

At the tertiary level, nurses frequently specialize in intensive care, cardiothoracic care, nephrology, oncology, or neonatology. They combine advanced clinical skills with evidence-based research and clinical instruction for student nurses. Regardless of the setting, nurses remain the central pillar ensuring patient advocacy, safety, and holistic support.
